note This setup names component ports, so its problem is built in a 3D view of the layout, made in memory as New 3D View from Layout makes one; nothing is written.
note U1: 23 shape(s) came from 5 placed instance(s), flattened into world coordinates for extraction.
note U1: 13 overlapping conductor shape(s) were merged into 3 — copper that overlaps on one level is one conductor, in 3D as in the planar model.
note U1: Robust meshing removed 3 of 51 outline points that lay within a fraction of a micrometre of the line through their neighbours; no outline moved by more than 0 µm.
note U1: Via barrels in this EM problem are solid: 'Plated Through-Hole' (Fill Plated, 25 µm wall) is built solid. A hollow barrel's air core changes nothing an RF answer can see and meshes into inverted elements; a thermal problem keeps the wall.
note U1: Placed in a 3D view, the layout's slabs are bounded by its board outline.
note The air box's floor is the underside of the ground plane at the bottom of the geometry, as a PEC face: the plane has no hole with other metal over it and lies under everything, so nothing below it carries field. State the AirBox's ZMin to pad below it instead.
